findings.title: Backup code plus any TOTP value skips the password
findings.body: In the credentials authorize() path, the password is verified only when credentials.totpCode is falsy (the existing check around the password branch). The new branch then accepts a backup code whenever credentials.backupCode is non-empty and never checks the TOTP value. A caller who knows only the email and one backup code can therefore sign in by also sending any non-empty totpCode (for example "000000") and omitting or faking the password. That makes a long-lived backup code a single factor and a full account takeover secret, instead of password plus backup code. The login UI happens to send an empty totpCode, but the public credentials endpoint does not. Password verification must run for CAL users on this path, and a dummy totpCode must not select the backup-code branch.

findings.title: Backup-code consumption is a lost-update race
findings.body: A matching backup code is marked used by reading the decrypted array, setting that index to null, and writing the whole blob back with a plain user update. Two overlapping logins can both read the same array before either write. If they present the same code, both pass the check and both sessions are created, so a one-time code works twice. If they present different codes, the later write overwrites the earlier one, so one consumed code is restored and can be reused. The update needs to be conditional on the previous ciphertext (or done under a row lock) so a stale write cannot resurrect a used code.

findings.title: Backup codes are compared case-sensitively
findings.body: Stored codes are lowercase hex (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")), but the login check uses indexOf on the raw string after only stripping "-". The same comparison is in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts around the backupCode.replaceAll call. The login field placeholder is "XXXXX-XXXXX", so a user who types the code in the casing the UI shows is rejected with incorrect backup code even though the code is valid. Normalize by trimming and lowercasing before compare on both login and disable.

findings.title: Backup codes are lost if the dialog is dismissed
findings.body: After TOTP enable succeeds, the only copy of the plaintext backup codes lives in this modal, and onEnable() runs only from the Close button. The Dialog is still wired to the parent's onOpenChange, so Escape, overlay click, or the dialog close control hides it without onEnable() and without any warning that the codes cannot be shown again. There is no later API to reveal or regenerate codes while 2FA stays on, and a refresh on this step drops them too. The settings switch can also stay off because the parent is never told enable finished, so the user is left with 2FA on server-side, no saved codes, and a UI that still looks disabled. This step should block dismiss until the user explicitly finishes, and that path must call onEnable().

findings.title: Download control submits the enable form
findings.body: The backup-code footer is inside the Form whose submit handler is handleEnable. Copy and Close call preventDefault because a click otherwise submits that form; the Download control does not, and its Button has no type="button". It is also wrapped in an anchor. Activating Download therefore posts the TOTP enable request again (which can error once 2FA is already on, or replace the page) and can cancel the file download, so the main way to save codes fails. Set type="button" and preventDefault, or render a non-submitting link.

findings.title: Lost access button submits the disable form
findings.body: The new Lost access / Go back button sits inside the disable Form and does not set type="button" or preventDefault. The enable modal in this same change had to preventDefault on footer buttons for that reason. Clicking Lost access therefore submits handleDisable with an empty code at the same time as it toggles the backup-code field, so the user gets an incorrect-code or second-factor error instead of a clean switch to the backup-code input. Stop the click from submitting.

findings.title: Missing-backup-codes copy points at a screen that does not exist
findings.body: missing_backup_codes says "Please generate them in your settings." Nothing in this PR adds a settings action to generate or rotate backup codes after 2FA is already on; setup refuses when twoFactorEnabled is true, and existing users who enabled 2FA before the migration have a null backupCodes column. Shown at login or when disabling 2FA, the message tells a locked-out user to do something they cannot do. The string should say that codes are only issued during 2FA setup and that an account with none cannot use this fallback.

findings.title: No test covers backup-code login or single use
findings.body: The new login and disable-with-backup-code paths are untested. The file's own TODO calls out login and disabling 2FA with a backup code, and the checklist says no test proves the feature. The enable test never clicks backup-codes-close or asserts the codes, and the other test only checks the download filename and that a toast appears, not the file contents, clipboard text, a successful backup-code sign-in, or that a used code is rejected. Those gaps would miss the password bypass, case-sensitive compare, and non-atomic consumption bugs.
